transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, my mind just keeps going completely blank at the absolute worst times. I'll be out there at work, and I'll look at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle... which, they actually gave us new paddles last month. They're supposed to be lighter, made of this weird aluminum stuff, but the handle gets freezing cold in the mornings. I tried wearing my wool gloves, the ones my sister knitted for me, but then I can't grip the radio right. She used this really scratchy purple yarn anyway, she always buys the cheap stuff from the craft store downtown. 

But... what was I saying? Right, the paddle. I'll just look at it, or the forms, and suddenly I cannot remember the steps I have done for years. Just gone. It’s like my brain just empties out. And then the traffic starts backing up, and people are honking, and I just stand there staring at the asphalt. They repaved that section of Route 9 back in October, and it already has potholes...
About when did you first start having these issues with your mind going blank?

I don't really know. Honestly, I can't give you a date. Time just sort of... slips away from me lately. I used to be so good at keeping track of things because I had this planner. It was a really nice leather-bound one I bought at that bookstore on Main Street, the one that closed down a few years ago. It was such a shame they closed, they had the best little cafe in the back. The barista—I think her name was Sarah, or maybe Samantha?—she always knew my order. Just a medium dark roast, nothing fancy. Now it's one of those boutique shops that sells overpriced candles that smell like pine needles and dirt. I went in there once and got a headache immediately from the smell. 

But anyway, what was the question? Oh, when the blankness started. Yeah, I really couldn't tell you. I just don't know. It feels like it just sort of snuck up on me.
Aside from these moments where your mind goes blank, how has your overall mood been lately?

It's been... bad. Really bad. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness right here in my chest. It's like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. And my bedroom floor is hardwood, you know? It gets so cold. I bought this rug, a big fluffy one, from a catalog my neighbor left in my mailbox by mistake. Her name is Mrs. Gable, she lives in the blue house on the corner. She always gets my mail and I get hers. Last week I got her electric bill. It was really high, but I guess she leaves her porch light on all night. It's one of those yellow bug lights, which I hate. They cast such a weird shadow on my driveway when I leave for work. 

But yeah, my mood... I just feel so sad. It's like I'm walking through mud all day.
Have there ever been times in your life when you felt the complete opposite—unusually energetic, hyper, or like you didn't need to sleep?

No, no, I've never felt like that. I'm always just so tired. Even when I try to sleep, I just lie there in the dark. I have these blackout curtains in my bedroom, because the streetlamp outside my window is so bright. It's one of those new LED ones the city installed last spring. They said it was supposed to save money and be better for the environment, but it's just blinding. It shines right through the crack in the curtains if I don't pin them shut with a binder clip. I have a whole box of those binder clips from when I was in college. I went to the state university, you know. I got my degree in communications. I thought I was going to work in public relations or maybe be a journalist. I used to write for the student paper. Mostly just opinion pieces about campus parking... the parking there was a nightmare. They oversold the permits every single semester. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Something about being hyper? No, I've never had that. Just the sadness and the tired.

I used to do so much. I really did. I was the one organizing all the choir rides at church, and the garden swaps in the neighborhood... oh, and the youth basketball snacks. I always made sure we had orange slices and those little juice boxes. The apple ones, not the fruit punch, because the fruit punch stains if they spill it on their jerseys. And you know how hard it is to get red dye out of polyester mesh? My sister-in-law told me to use baking soda and vinegar, but honestly, it just makes the laundry room smell like a science fair project. I remember doing a volcano project in fifth grade with my dad. We used papier-mâché and painted it brown and green. He got paint on his favorite flannel shirt and my mom was so mad. It was that red and black plaid one he wore every time he raked the leaves. 

But... yeah. Now I just... I can sit for hours just staring at my phone. I don't even open any apps, just stare at the screen. People text me, the choir director, the other moms, and I just... I don't feel the push to answer anybody. I just don't care anymore.
Have you had any recent physical medical illnesses or head injuries?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been sick or hit my head or anything. I did get a really bad sunburn last summer, though. I was working my corner—I'm a crossing guard over by the elementary school on Elm Street—and I forgot my hat. It's this wide-brimmed straw hat I got at a craft fair three years ago. The woman who made it was selling all these beautiful hand-woven baskets, too. I almost bought one to keep my knitting yarn in, but I ended up getting the hat instead because it had this pretty blue ribbon around it. Blue is my favorite color. My first car was blue. It was a Honda Civic, a '98 I think. The heater didn't work right, so I had to keep a blanket in the backseat during the winter. It was one of those scratchy wool blankets you get at an army surplus store. My uncle used to shop at those places all the time. He collected old canteens... 

But no, no medical problems or head injuries. Just the sunburn, but that healed up fine.
Has this feeling of sadness and lack of interest been going on nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Two weeks? Oh, no, it's been so much longer than that. This heavy feeling... the guilt, the just having no energy and not even wanting to eat... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. I remember because it started right around the time the grocery store down the street changed their layout. They moved the bakery section to the front, right by the sliding doors. I used to go in just to smell the bread. My grandmother used to bake bread every Sunday. Sourdough, mostly. She kept her starter in this old glass jar on top of the fridge. She said the warmth from the fridge helped it grow. She had that fridge for like twenty years, one of those almond-colored ones from the eighties. It had a handle that you had to pull really hard to open, and the seal was kind of sticky. We put all my report cards on it with these little magnetic alphabet letters. I think I lost the letter 'J' somewhere under the stove... 

But yeah, it's been over a year. A year and two months of feeling like this every single day.
